name: Hermès
why: Leather goods, silk and clothing made in the company's own workshops, with no licensees.
origin: Founded in Paris in 1837 by Thierry Hermès as a harness maker.

notes.craft: Hermès's 2025 Universal Registration Document reports 79 owned production sites and 55% of output from in-house and exclusive workshops, centred on leather goods, tanneries, silk/textiles and other métiers. It names no owned ready-to-wear site, and men's PDPs mostly say 'Made in Italy' with no maker named. Owned making covers a large part of the house but not demonstrably the clothing, so 4 for a clothing score.
notes.status: the terminal status brand — waitlists as architecture
notes.finbro: the H belt as bonus-day announcement
notes.racquet: Grass and clay rather than a squash court behind a mahogany door. The register is a lawn in summer, and the house has the equestrian vocabulary to match.
notes.boat: Sailing sits inside a house that began with harnesses, so the register arrives through leather and craft rather than through marine function. Cashmere on deck, and someone else at the helm.

craft_evidence.owned_d: Group (Hermès International, brand = group) says it operates '79 fully owned production and training sites, including 63 in France', and '55% manufactured in its in-house and exclusive workshops' (2025 URD, pp.18, 26). Owned métiers listed: leather goods and saddlery, tanneries, silk/textiles, shoes, crystal, porcelain, jewellery, perfume, watches. The URD text read does not identify any site for ready-to-wear or menswear, and does not say RTW is made in-house; leather goods also use 'a network of long-standing French partners'.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 3/5, France 2/5 (sample of 5 men's PDPs on hermes.com: overshirt H662210HD87 Italy, C.D.S. crewneck sweater H657770HA90 Italy, Malte pants H665840H801 Italy, straight-cut jeans H665400H802 France, rib-trim jacket H652330HE02 France).
